title: Muslim-Violence Bias Persists in Debiased GPT Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the tendency of Large Language Models to generate violent completions when prompted with text containing religious identifiers (generic terms like 'Muslim') versus common names associated with specific religions. It specifically measures anti-Muslim bias compared to other religious groups by analyzing the rate and themes of violent text generation.
findings: While InstructGPT showed reduced anti-Muslim bias in generic prompts compared to GPT-3, significant bias persisted when using common names associated with Islam (second-order bias). ChatGPT exhibited a much stronger explicit bias than InstructGPT in generic conditions and comparable high levels of bias in name-based conditions, suggesting that recent model developments may have mitigated the effects of previous de-biasing efforts regarding Muslim-violence associations.
